questions.q: In the scenario, why does Change A (the label and validation-message fix) qualify for a Standard Change template?
options: Because the CAB does not review any UI-related changes
Because all pipeline deployments automatically qualify for Standard Change templates
It has narrow functional scope and direct, passing ATF test coverage of exactly what changed
Because it was the first PR merged that week
questions.explain: The combination of a small, well-understood scope and specific test evidence is what justifies the pre-approved fast path.

questions.q: Why does Change B (the approval routing logic) still warrant full CAB review despite passing its ATF suite?
options: Because approval routing changes are never allowed to deploy at all
Because server-side tests are considered unreliable and should be ignored
Because Change B's pipeline actually failed to build
Because passing tests prove technical correctness against what was tested, not that the business risk of an approval-routing mistake is low
questions.explain: Approval routing above a dollar threshold carries real financial and audit consequences that a passing test suite doesn't, by itself, rule out.

questions.q: What role does ServiceNow DevOps play once each pull request's pipeline reaches its deploy stage?
options: It blocks the deployment from happening until a human manually approves the code
It rewrites the application's business rules automatically
It receives the deploy event and creates or updates the corresponding Change Request with real pipeline-run details
It has no role at the deploy stage, only at the build stage
questions.explain: This is the same mechanism Lessons 17 and 18 covered — the deploy event is what generates or updates the governed Change Request.

questions.q: What was the actual deciding factor between routing Change A versus Change B differently?
options: Which pull request was opened first
Whether the pipeline build succeeded, which was true for both
The number of lines of code changed in each pull request
What the change actually touched, and whether the passing test coverage was evidence about the part of the system carrying the business risk
questions.explain: Both changes had a clean build and a fully passing ATF suite — the difference was scope and what the risk actually was.

questions.q: What does this lab demonstrate about applying Lesson 19's risk-based thinking in practice?
options: Risk-based differentiation only applies to applications without any automated tests
The same application and pipeline can correctly produce both a fast Standard Change and a CAB-reviewed Normal Change in the same week
Every change from a well-tested pipeline should always get the same routing
ATF coverage makes CAB review unnecessary for any application
questions.explain: Risk-based differentiation means evaluating each change on its own merits, not applying one blanket rule to every pipeline-driven change.
